description: The flat-topped thorn tree of the Serengeti's plains and woodland edges, 5-12 m tall and often twice as wide, a dark fissured trunk forking low into ascending limbs that carry a thin umbrella of tiny feathery leaves. Paired thorns, one long straight and white, one short hooked and dark, guard every twig, and the coiled pods fall in the dry season.

season_notes.winter: December to February, after the short rains: in full leaf, fresh green, the fragrant white puffball flowers finishing.
season_notes.spring: March to May, the long rains: dense grey-green leaf over green grass; pods forming.
season_notes.summer: June to August, the dry season: leaves thinning and yellowing, the coiled pods ripening and dropping; giraffe, elephants and impala gather under the trees for them.
season_notes.fall: September to November: the thinnest crowns of the year on the driest ground, then a new flush and the white flowers ahead of the short rains.

targets.from: judgement values from the drafter's reading of the sources and knowledge of the species (2026-11-05), no photographs measured; to be replaced by photo measurements: a short dark trunk forking low into a few ascending limbs that spread into a flat, wide, thin umbrella of fine grey-green foliage, much wider than tall

notes: Grown from western redbud (the library's only tree-like legume, a Troll-model vase like the acacias) as a single tree: the trunk forks low (split at 0.4 of its length into three limbs) and the first branch level is long and nearly horizontal at the top, clipped by a flat, wide envelope (radius 0.88 of the height) into the umbrella. This is untested in the lineup and the generator's envelope fit may round the top. COMPROMISES: the leaves are bipinnate with tiny leaflets (pinnae 4-10 pairs, each with up to 15 pairs of leaflets, the leaf about 2.5 cm, Wikipedia); the generator has no bipinnate leaf, so they are drawn as tiny pinnate leaves, which reads as a fine texture at distance only. The paired thorns are not drawn at all (there is no spine primitive). The coiled, spring-like pods are drawn as pale brown berry clusters. Leaf loss in the dry season is a leaf_on_by_month curve (lowest in September), the drafter's judgement: the species is semi-deciduous, never fully bare in the Serengeti. The client's seasons are calendar quarters (winter Dec-Feb, spring Mar-May, summer Jun-Aug, fall Sep-Nov) whatever the hemisphere or climate; the colours and leaf-on here are given for those months at the tile, not for a temperate winter. The flowering months (October to December, ahead of and in the short rains) are the drafter's knowledge and vary by year. Browsers: giraffe browse it year round (the trees' flat tops are partly their work), elephants break branches and eat pods, impala and baboons take fallen pods (the drafter's knowledge; Wikipedia says only that pods and foliage feed desert grazers). None of these animals is in the library yet; the ids are GBIF binomials so games.py links them when they arrive. Leopards rest and cache kills in acacias (cover_for). Region tag east_africa is not yet a natural region in pipeline/regions.py.
